stories.headline: Broncos Rally Past Jaguars 20-13 in Home Opener Behind Nix, Waddle
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos overcame a sluggish first half and a 13-3 deficit to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 Sunday at Empower Field at Mile High, picking up their first win of the 2026 season. Quarterback Bo Nix posted a second-half passing line of 11-for-15 for 132 yards and a touchdown, while new receiver Jaylen Waddle finished with eight catches for 138 yards in his home debut.

Rookie running back Jonah Coleman stepped up with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey both exiting with injuries, carrying 10 times and scoring the game-clinching touchdown. The Broncos outscored Jacksonville 17-3 in the second half, with cornerback Riley Moss providing a pivotal interception of Trevor Lawrence late in the game.

Despite the win, penalties remained a concern — Denver was flagged 10 times, including a call that wiped out a Nik Bonitto sack-fumble in the first quarter. The defense rebounded sharply from its collapse in Kansas City, limiting the Jaguars to just 95 total yards and sacking Lawrence twice.

The win gave Denver 15 victories in its last 17 games with Nix at quarterback. Dobbins' reported hamstring injury adds uncertainty at running back heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

stories.headline: Rockies Drop Series to Mariners, One Loss From Fourth Straight 100-Loss Season
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies fell 2-1 to the Seattle Mariners on Sunday at Coors Field, dropping the three-game series and pushing their loss total to 99 on the season. The defeat leaves the Rockies needing to go 6-0 over their final two series to avoid their fourth consecutive 100-loss season — a threshold that would place them among only five franchises in MLB history to suffer four straight such seasons.

Colorado received strong pitching from Tomoyuki Sugano (five innings, one run) and Ryan Feltner in long relief (three innings, one run), but the offense managed just one run, a ninth-inning home run by Hunter Goodman, his 39th of the year. The Rockies went 0-for-5 with runners in scoring position and stranded six runners.

Since Aug. 17, Colorado is 7-25 with only one series win, ranking near the bottom of the league in clutch hitting during that stretch. The team is 17-25 in one-run games and 39-47 in games decided by two runs or fewer this season.

The Rockies close out their home schedule with a three-game series against Arizona beginning Tuesday, then travel to face the Chicago White Sox for their final road series. The looming MLB labor dispute adds further uncertainty to the franchise's offseason outlook.

stories.headline: Golden Gate Canyon State Park Becomes Colorado's First Urban Night Sky Place
stories.summary:
Golden Gate Canyon State Park has received Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International, making it the first Colorado state park to earn that specific recognition. The designation acknowledges the park's ongoing efforts to reduce metropolitan light pollution in support of wildlife and habitat conservation.

Park staff replaced or retrofitted 96 light fixtures, expanded education programming aligned with DarkSky principles, and forged partnerships with local astronomy groups. The park also hosts regular stargazing events open to the public.

Golden Gate Canyon is the second Colorado state park recognized by DarkSky International overall, following Jackson Lake State Park, which received International Dark Sky Park status in 2020. The application process began in 2024 in collaboration with the Colorado Tourism Office and DarkSky Colorado.

DarkSky International works globally to preserve dark nighttime environments for ecological and cultural reasons. The designation is expected to draw additional visitors interested in astronomy and night-sky recreation to the park, located west of Golden in Jefferson County.

stories.headline: Driverless Waymo Cruises Through South Pearl Street Farmers Market During Setup
stories.summary:
A Waymo autonomous vehicle navigated into the South Pearl Street Farmers Market during vendor setup Sunday morning, drawing startled reactions from merchants and drawing wide attention after a local bakery posted video of the incident to social media. The car traveled slowly along a path intended for pedestrian foot traffic, at one point turning toward people near vendor tents before stopping.

Farmers Market coordinator Marilyn Kahlich said no one was hurt and there was no property damage, though organizers were unsure how to stop or redirect the vehicle and resorted to following it while warning others in its path. Kahlich noted the Waymo was traveling in the correct direction of vendor setup flow.

A Waymo spokesperson said the vehicle was already en route to a destination on South Pearl Street when the market setup began, and that the car quickly identified the situation and maneuvered out of the area. The South Pearl Farmers Market runs from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. every third Sunday between May and November.

The incident highlights ongoing questions about how autonomous vehicles interact with temporary and unplanned urban environments. Waymo has been operating its driverless taxi service in Denver in a limited capacity.

stories.headline: 13-Year-Old Girl Missing From Unincorporated Adams County Since Saturday
stories.summary:
Adams County law enforcement and the Colorado Bureau of Investigation are searching for a 13-year-old girl, Jody Hunt, who was last seen Saturday afternoon in unincorporated Adams County north of Denver. She was reported missing near the 3100 block of West 68th Avenue at approximately 3 p.m. and is the subject of an endangered missing alert.

Hunt is described as 5-foot-2 and 100 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes. She was last seen wearing pink flannel pajama pants and black Nike sneakers.

The Colorado Bureau of Investigation issued the alert Sunday, urging the public to contact the Adams County Sheriff's Office at 303-288-1535 with any information on Hunt's whereabouts. Anyone who sees her is also asked to call 911.

The investigation is ongoing and authorities have not released further details about the circumstances of her disappearance.

stories.headline: Pickup Driver Dies in Suspected DUI Crash With Semi-Truck in Wheat Ridge
stories.summary:
A pickup truck driver died Friday evening following a crash with a semi-truck in Wheat Ridge, according to the Wheat Ridge Police Department. Officers received a report of the crash at approximately 6:55 p.m., and the pickup driver was later pronounced dead at the hospital. The semi-truck driver was not injured.

Preliminary investigation indicates the pickup swerved into oncoming traffic before the collision, police said. Officers found open containers in the pickup, and authorities said DUI may be a contributing factor.

The department's crash and traffic investigation team is handling the case. Portions of the affected roadway were closed for several hours before reopening around midnight.

The identity of the deceased driver has not been publicly released. No charges have been announced as the investigation continues.

stories.headline: Denver Oktoberfest Ranked Among Top 10 Best in the U.S. by USA Today
stories.summary:
Denver Oktoberfest has been named one of the 10 best Oktoberfest celebrations in the United States by USA Today's 10Best readers' choice program, landing in seventh place. The annual event draws an estimated 350,000 attendees and spans two weekends in September.

The celebration features German food, beer, commemorative steins and entertainment including wiener dog racing, keg bowling and stein hoisting competitions. The event highlights German heritage and culture for the Denver metro area.

The USA Today 10Best rankings are determined through a combination of expert panel selections and public voting. Zeeco Oktoberfest Tulsa in Tulsa, Oklahoma, took the top spot nationally.

Denver Oktoberfest's inclusion on the national list underscores the event's standing as one of the region's largest cultural festivals. Details on remaining 2026 event dates are available through event organizers.

stories.headline: Injured Dirt Bike Rider Rescued by Multiagency Team in Douglas County
stories.summary:
An injured dirt bike rider was rescued Saturday evening on Trail 679 near Jackson Creek in the Rampart Range area of Douglas County, according to Douglas County Search and Rescue. ATV, ground and drone teams were immediately deployed alongside Douglas County Fire Helitack, which searched from the air.

The drone team located the rider, confirmed their position and communicated with them via the drone's loudspeaker, informing them that help was on the way. Crews also observed that the rider had built a small fire to stay warm, which was relayed to responding ground teams.

Medics and ATV crews reached the rider and administered initial medical treatment before determining helicopter transport was necessary. HCA Healthone AirLife transported the rider to a higher level of care from a nearby landing zone.

Douglas County Search and Rescue emphasized the importance of not riding alone in remote areas. In this case, the rider's partner called for help, provided an accurate location and helped keep the injured person warm until rescuers arrived.

stories.headline: One Man's RV Park and Tiny Home Village Aims to Revive Fading Eastern Plains Town of Arriba
stories.summary:
Ben VanderWerf, a contractor-turned-entrepreneur, is building a 65-site RV park and 33-pad tiny home community in Arriba, a Lincoln County town of roughly 300 residents located about 70 miles from the Kansas border off Interstate 70. VanderWerf opened Big Ben's RV Park and Tiny Home Community in 2023 after leasing a dormant campground at the base of the town's highway exit ramp and has since grown it into a functioning community.

Much of the early business has come from traveling workers tied to the wind, solar and pipeline construction boom on the Eastern Plains, including crews working on ONEOK's 230-mile fuel pipeline from Kansas to Denver International Airport and Xcel Energy's new transmission lines. VanderWerf said the park is now mostly full and a new clubhouse is nearing completion.

The tiny home portion of the development aims to offer affordable housing at $650 per month, including utilities and internet, for families looking to live simply. VanderWerf and his family live in a 550-square-foot tiny home prototype he built in 2021.

Not all Arriba residents support the project, though skepticism is notable given the struggles faced by many Eastern Plains communities. VanderWerf's effort offers a case study in whether small-scale entrepreneurship and the region's energy development boom can breathe new life into remote rural Colorado towns.

stories.headline: Six Aurora Teens to Face Charges Following August 'Teen Takeover' Near Del Mar Park
stories.summary:
Six Aurora teenagers are set to face charges stemming from an August incident dubbed a 'teen takeover' near Del Mar Park, authorities announced. The event involved a large gathering of youths that drew significant law enforcement response.

Details on the specific charges have not been fully disclosed, but authorities indicated the cases will move forward through the juvenile justice system. The incident drew community concern about public safety and youth behavior in the Aurora area.

The Aurora Police Department and city officials have not specified whether additional suspects remain under investigation. The August gathering was one of several similar events reported in metro Denver communities over the summer.

City and community leaders have been discussing responses to such organized gatherings, including increased patrols and youth engagement programs. The cases against the six teens are expected to proceed in coming weeks.

stories.headline: Governor Polis Signs Executive Order to Protect Pollinators Across Colorado
stories.summary:
Governor Jared Polis signed an executive order directing state agencies to take coordinated action to protect pollinators, including bees, butterflies and other insects critical to Colorado's agricultural and natural ecosystems. The order signals a statewide policy commitment to addressing pollinator population declines driven by habitat loss, pesticide use and climate change.

The executive order instructs relevant state departments to assess pollinator habitats on state-managed lands, reduce harmful pesticide applications where feasible and promote pollinator-friendly land management practices. It also calls for increased public education on pollinator conservation.

Colorado agriculture depends heavily on pollinators, with billions of dollars in crop production tied to bee and insect activity each year. Advocates for the order say it establishes a framework for more systematic protection that goes beyond previous voluntary efforts.

Details on implementation timelines and specific agency responsibilities are expected to follow as departments develop action plans. The order does not require legislative approval.

stories.headline: Eastern Colorado's World's Wonder View Tower Marks 100th Anniversary With Artist Renovation and Saturday Celebration
stories.summary:
The World's Wonder View Tower in Genoa, Colorado, celebrated its 100th anniversary Saturday with a community event and an artist-led renovation of the historic roadside attraction on the Eastern Plains. The tower, located off Interstate 70 in Lincoln County, has stood as a quirky landmark drawing curious travelers since the 1920s.

The renovation involved local and regional artists working to restore and reimagine elements of the tower and its surrounding museum of oddities. Organizers framed the project as an effort to preserve the site's legacy while attracting new visitors to the rural community.

The World's Wonder View Tower is known for its eclectic collection of curiosities and claims of panoramic views spanning multiple states from its top. It has long served as a cultural touchstone for Eastern Plains communities and road-trip travelers along the I-70 corridor.

The centennial celebration drew visitors from across the region and reflects broader efforts to promote tourism and economic activity in Colorado's rural eastern corridor, where many small towns have faced long-term population and economic decline.

topStory.headline: CNN, MSNBC, Politico Sue White House After Trump Bans Outlets From Press Coverage
topStory.summary:
CNN, MSNBC and Politico are preparing a First Amendment lawsuit against the Trump administration after President Donald Trump announced Friday that he was banning the three news organizations from the White House. Reporters from all three outlets were turned away at White House security kiosks Saturday and had their credentials revoked. Trump announced the ban on his Truth Social platform, citing what he called "constant" reporting of "FAKE NEWS" and warning that other outlets could face similar action.

The dispute escalated Sunday night when the White House removed CNN from its scheduled role as the primary television pool representative for the entire White House press corps on Monday, breaking with decades of established precedent. Under a long-standing arrangement, ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News rotate the television pool responsibility, with a single crew supplying footage used by news organizations worldwide. The White House's Sunday scheduling email omitted any primary TV network and instead listed Real America's Voice, a small pro-Trump outlet, as the secondary crew for Trump's trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

Sen. John Barrasso, R-Wyo., appearing Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press," declined to say whether the ban violated the First Amendment, instead arguing that "the press has an obligation to report fairly." Barrasso drew a comparison to Trump's own prior bans from Twitter and Facebook, saying, "I didn't see people come to his defense," and added that he did not believe the controversy would affect Republicans in the midterm elections 44 days away. Gabe Rottman, vice president of policy for the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said flatly the ban was not legal.

The removal of CNN from the television pool carries consequences well beyond CNN's own newsroom, as pool footage serves as the primary means by which the public and media worldwide see the president during limited-access events and travel. It remains unclear how the other four major networks will respond to CNN's exclusion or how pool coverage will be handled during Trump's New York trip. Media critics have called on the networks to show public solidarity with the banned outlets as the legal challenge moves forward.
